abstract: Lighting is as much an art as it is a science and this may be the reason why lighting engineers find themselves so often as a body apart from engineers in general. articleTitle: Economies in the use of protective relays
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper attempts to explode the myth that a cheaper relay is the most economical since the overall cost of the relay, engineering and other incidental expenses must be considered. The most economical scheme may well be the one where the more expensive biased relay is used instead of the less expensive unbiased relay. The biased relay should be preferred as long as it is of simple construction and avoids complicated circuits with a multiplicity of contacts. Its high-speed feature, due to inherent stability, affords bettor protection. Engineering time and, therefore, money is saved if calculations can be positive and reliable in the first instance so that finality can be reached immediately without the need for any special proving tests. Standardization of relay elements, cases, etc., can help to reduce maintenance time since this avoids a wide knowledge of many different types of movement. The ease of testing is discussed in relation to special test facilities. All those factors must be taken into account if the most economical scheme is to be chosen.

articleTitle: A review of methods of starting induction motors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The normal methods of starting induction motors are well known but the theory of these methods is usually taken for granted. This paper is an attempt to supply in simple form a practical theory directly applicable to the majority of everyday problems and compare the various methods of starting commonly employed. Theoretical accuracy has been sacrificed to practical utility and simplicity. It is hoped that the result will appeal to the practicing engineer. The stickler for accuracy and mathematical exactitude is warned that this paper is not for him. The general induction motor theory is reduced to a theory of the rotor current and torque. Direct-on-line and star-delta starting are considered and the load-torque-speed limitation of the latter noted. Devices for use in the stator circuit are reviewed in some detail and compared. Devices for use in the rotor circuit are similarly reviewed and compared. Finally, a new method of designing a rotor starting resistance is described.

articleTitle: Design features of insulators and transformers which contribute to radio interffrence from power lines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is based upon a thesis submitted to the University of Natal for the degree of M.Sc. in the Department of Electrical Engineering SUMMARY This paper deals with the investigation into the causes of radio interference radiated from power lines on the Natal Central System of the Electricity Supply Commission. It is shown that the interference is due to the ionization of small pockets of air associated with insulating material. The occurrence of highly-stressed air gaps on power systems is considered with respect to line insulators and transformers, and methods of testing for radio interference are suggested.

abstract: As the subject of meter testing is highly specialized, the paper first classifies and reviews the various methods of measuring the errors of a.c. kilowatt-hour meters. A description is then given of new equipment for rapid and precise testing in which decade counter tubes, controlled by a rotary sub-standard, are used to indicate the error. The substandard runs at the same speed on both unity and 0.5 power factor. Starting and stopping of the counter is effected with high precision without any mechanical movement. This is accomplished by optical and electronic means involving clip-on mirrors which are attached to the meter spindles by special tools. Push-button load selection, error tables and meter connecting plugs are employed. The results obtained and costs involved are given. A new device for preliminary setting of the quadrature and low-load adjustments is described; also a new dial-testing machine. Starting load-tests, creep tests and warming facilities are briefly discussed. Finally, the application of the electronic test method to the calibration of rotary substandards is mentioned.
